proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr X_0=\sigma(z_0,E_0)\).  By \texttt{def:target} and linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid\mathscr X_0]
-n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid\mathscr X_0]
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} and the definition of \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) give
\[
n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid\mathscr X_0]
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0].
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-transport} gives
\[
n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid\mathscr X_0]
=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (2)--(3) into (1) proves the identifying equality.  Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-regression} separately establishes that \(m_s\) is the observed-law conditional regression learned from untreated pseudo-event blocks.  Thus the equality between the causal target and the observed-law functional follows from consistency and event transport; it is not imposed by definition.

Fix a successful pair \((s,k)\), abbreviate \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\bar B_s\), and fix \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  The event part of the criterion in \texttt{def:fwl-regression} satisfies
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^{\top}\gamma)^2
=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s)^2
+(\bar B_s-\theta-e_0^{\top}\gamma)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(\gamma\), the unique minimizing event coefficient is consequently
\[
\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\gamma.
\tag{5}
\]
At (5), the event criterion is independent of \(\gamma\), so the profiled criterion, apart from the first constant in (4), is
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}
\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\gamma\}^2.
\tag{6}
\]
This is exactly the historical weighted least-squares problem in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Passage of the selected normalized Gram-shape test implies \(G_{sk}\succ0\), hence (6) has the unique selected minimizer \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\).  Thus
\[
\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}.
\tag{7}
\]
Finally, using the definitions of \(\widehat m_s\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}\), and \(\widehat\tau\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}
&=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}
 (\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk})\\
&=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)
=\widehat\tau.
\end{aligned}
\]
This identity is algebraic on every sample on which all selected fits exist.

Fix a regular conditional law given \(E_0\), and put
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
All constants below are chosen in the nonempty interior of the fixed support, variance, Holder, covariance, and modulus envelopes.  Place the query in a fixed compact subset of the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\) contained in \(\mathcal Z_+\).  Draw event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\), and, conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw historical errors independently across units with conditional mean zero.  Then
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means are \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, and make every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  This verifies \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  Bounded two-point response kernels with probabilities in a fixed compact subset of \((0,1)\) verify both wealth bounds and \texttt{ass:response-variance}, after choosing the fixed envelopes compatibly.  Draw donors conditionally independently and identically, independently of the panel, with covariance and standardized fourth moment strictly inside the declared envelopes, and set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Equation (8) verifies the two extra full-design restrictions.  Hence each experiment constructed below is a regular conditional causal-panel law in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

For later use, if \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), Taylor's theorem applied to Bernoulli relative entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le \frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Conditional product structure makes the divergence of the response law the sum of the conditional binary divergences.

For the treated channel, write \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and change the event response probability in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\); a sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\) keeps all probabilities in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The target separation and divergence satisfy
\[
\sum_s\pi_sv_s=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{10}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), put
\[
b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)},
\]
and, for a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump \(\psi\) with \(\psi(0)=1\), perturb only cohort \(s_*\) by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b).
\tag{11}
\]
For \(\lambda>1\), use a common affine carrier with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient; for \(0<\lambda\le1\), use a common asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier.  Taking \(c_1\) sufficiently small preserves the response interior, the Holder radius, and both sides of the local-modulus inequality.  Since \(S\) is fixed and the design density is bounded above,
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\ge cR_{\mathrm{sm}},
\tag{12}
\]
and (9), integrated over a support of probability at most \(Cb^d\), yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{13}
\]

For the spacing channel take the pair constructed in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  It satisfies (8), the one-time density bounds, the frozen geometric mixing envelope, and the two-sided local modulus.  Its observed laws coincide on a no-active-block event having probability bounded away from zero, and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge c\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus this pair has positive testing affinity; no Kullback--Leibler bound is claimed for it.

For the donor channel retain the same affine or asymmetric-cusp carrier.  By the lower local-modulus inequality, for \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\le\delta_0\), the definition of the supremum supplies an admissible \(u_N\), chosen to attain at least one half of the supremum, such that
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2\le c_2N^{-1/2},
\quad
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
Use a fixed common-support finite distribution on \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\) whose support affinely spans \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\), whose covariance lies strictly inside the ellipticity envelope, and whose atom probabilities lie strictly inside the probability simplex.  Perturb the atom probabilities along a bounded score whose induced mean shift is \(u_N\).  The spanning and interior properties make this possible for all sufficiently small \(u_N\); shrinking \(c_2\) preserves the covariance and fourth-moment envelopes.  Taylor expansion of the finite probability-vector likelihood, whose Hessian is bounded on that compact simplex neighborhood, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{16}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete untreated event potential outcomes under each law with cohort means \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (15) into a target separation whose square is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

It remains to turn the three divergence bounds into affinity.  For any two laws, data processing under the test \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), followed by the elementary binary Pinsker inequality, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\ge2\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2.
\]
The binary inequality follows by twice differentiating binary relative entropy, whose second derivative is at least four.  Therefore
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{17}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (17) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and donor pairs; (14) supplies affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (9) verify membership in the same full-design-centered class for all four pairs, proving every assertion.

For channel \(q\), take the pair \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, write its two target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  The pair has affinity at least \(a_0>0\) and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\), where \(R_q=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in the spacing channel.  For any estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the two sets
\[
E_0'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E_1'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E_0')+P_{1,q}(E_1')\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge \frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{18}
\]
Maximizing over the four channels, then taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and the infimum over estimators, proves the lower bound \(cR_{\star,\beta}\).

For the upper bound let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \(\mathscr X,E_0\), and the donor sample.  Since \(z_0\) is \(E_0\)-measurable, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation of the successful local-polynomial fits give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{19}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\(B_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is the Taylor remainder around the fold centers, and \(B_{\mathrm{don}}\) is the fold-averaged weighted-surface difference between those centers and \(z_0\).

The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under the displayed conditioning.  Conditional cross-unit independence and the range bound \(B\) yield
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\tag{20}
\]
and \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{21}
\]
This treats each unit's complete calendar history as one cluster and assumes no temporal independence inside it.

If \(C_K\) bounds the Euclidean radius of the support of \(K\), then \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2\le C_Kh_{sk}\) wherever \(w_{stk}>0\).  The deterministic weight bound and the Holder Taylor remainder give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_kh_{sk}^{\lambda}.
\tag{22}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\).  Since \(S\) and \(K_D\) are fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz in (22) gives, on the good sample,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{23}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\) because \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\) and \(N\ge1\).

For a donor complement of size \(m_k\), independence and expansion of the fourth moment give
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left\{m_k^{-1}\sum_{j\notin k}Z_j-z_0\right\}
\right\|_2^4\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le Cm_k^{-2}.
\tag{24}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive in Euclidean norm; donor ellipticity changes (24) only by a fixed factor when it is expressed in the covariance norm.  On the event that this norm is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds the squared fold discrepancy by a constant times its \(2\kappa\)-th power.  Lyapunov's inequality applied to (24) bounds its expectation by \(Cm_k^{-\kappa}\).  On the complementary event, boundedness of the surfaces and Markov's inequality applied to (24) give \(Cm_k^{-2}\).  Since \(K_D\) is fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{25}
\]

On every successful fit the fitted intercept has absolute value at most \(B\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2}\), while failed intercepts are set to zero.  Hence squared error is bounded by a fixed constant on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes this contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  The inequality \((x_1+\cdots+x_4)^2\le4\sum_jx_j^2\), together with (19)--(25), proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{26}
\]
This is also an upper bound for the minimax infimum because \(\widehat\tau\) is a single data-measurable estimator.

For completeness put \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\).  Weighted arithmetic--geometric mean gives
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
After multiplication by \(\pi_s^2\) and summation,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}+T^{-2\lambda/d}
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}.
\tag{27}
\]
Thus smoothing is a bookkeeping component but is never uniquely active.  Equations (18) and (26) establish the asserted same-class bracket for every relative-growth array.  Spectral clipping makes \(\widehat\Sigma\) feasible, while neither the estimator nor (24) requires Gaussianity or homoskedasticity.

Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \(\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\).  On every successful fit, the normal equations and nonsingularity of \(G_{sk}\) imply polynomial reproduction:
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{stik}p(u_{stk})=p(0)
\]
for every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(r\).  Applying this identity to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\), and then applying \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}, gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk}
-m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
-\sum_{t,i}a_{stik}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{28}
\]
After cohort weighting and fold averaging, the right side of (28) is exactly \(A_L\).

Define
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} centers \(U_{si}\) conditionally on the displayed sigma-field, and \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables independent over \((s,i)\).  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|.
\]
For a centered variable in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of the exponential bounds its conditional moment generating function by the endpoint mixture with the same mean; direct differentiation gives \(\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\cdot]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}\).  Multiplication over units, Chernoff's inequality, and optimization over \(v>0\) therefore give
\[
P\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{29}
\]

Likewise define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers these variables conditionally on \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence preserves this centering after donors are included.  Conditional cross-unit independence makes them independent across units, and their range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same exponential calculation yields
\[
P\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{30}
\]
No independence between a unit's event outcome and its historical path is used; (29) and (30) are combined by Bonferroni.

For donor fold \(k\), put \(m=m_k\) and \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-replication} gives independent mean-zero vectors with \(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding the fourth power and retaining the index patterns in which every centered vector occurs at least twice yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|m^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
&=m^{-1}\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1m\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le \frac Bm+\left(1-\frac1m\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
Markov's inequality at \(q_k\) gives conditional failure probability at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}/K_D\).  Coordinatewise projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), which lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds then imply on the calibrated event
\[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\{\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0\}
\right\|_2
\le \sqrt{\frac{C_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}}\frac{q_k}{\sqrt{m_k}}
=\delta_k.
\tag{32}
\]
A union bound over the fixed donor folds has error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\).  On the good sample \(\delta_k\le\delta_0\), so the upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (32) give
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_k^\kappa.
\tag{33}
\]
Fold averaging turns (33) into the allowance \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).

By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the full-data raw-estimator error is the event fluctuation in (30), minus the historical fluctuation in (29), minus the Taylor remainder in (28), and minus the generated-center discrepancy in (33).  Since
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha,
\]
Bonferroni gives, on the good sample,
\[
P\{|widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\le H_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{34}
\]
On the bad sample \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\), and \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) by \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth} and the convex cohort weights.  Thus (34) proves uniform conditional coverage.  It uses neither studentization nor a lower event-outcome variance.

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives deterministically on every successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\quad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{35}
\]
The kernel support and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_kh_{sk}^\lambda.
\]
The \(a=\lambda\) moment bound in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control}, the fixed values of \(S,K_D\), and Cauchy--Schwarz across cohorts imply
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{36}
\]
Since \(D,S,K_D\) are fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\), (31) makes \(q_k\) uniformly bounded, so
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{37}
\]
The selector lemma bounds the bad-sample probability by \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  The fallback interval has length at most \(2B\), and eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  As \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on the good sample, (35)--(37) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{38}
\]

For the lower bound, reduce the fixed perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so every channel affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for a fixed \(a_0>0\).  For the rare-block pair this is achieved by decreasing its fixed active-block intensity, without changing its rate order.  Let \(I\) be uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's target values, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\).  Uniform honesty and domination by the two laws imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge \mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{39}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{40}
\]
Maximizing (40) over the four channels gives \(c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Combining (34), (38), and (40) proves the claimed same-class coverage and expected-length bracket along every stated array.

Under the first specialization, \(S=1\) and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) imply \(\pi_1=1\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) give
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_1(z_{01})
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-z_{01}-\Delta_0.
\tag{41}
\]
When the proxy is the event cohort's baseline outcome, \(z_{01}\) is its conditional baseline mean.  When \(\Delta_0\) is the untreated cohort-average post-minus-baseline mean change, (41) is treated post minus treated baseline minus the untreated post-minus-baseline change, namely the canonical conditional finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences contrast.

For the second specialization define
\[
\tau_s=n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Homogeneity across cohorts means \(\tau_s=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\) for every \(s\).  By \texttt{def:target} and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\tau_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}.
\tag{42}
\]
The stipulated absence of carry-over beyond \(h=0\) makes the common terminal-level contrast in (42) the contemporaneous finite-cohort effect on the buy-and-hold wealth level in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}; the causal interpretation comes from that stipulation, not from the algebra.

Suppress \((s,k)\), write \(\mathsf L=L_{sk}\) and \(G=G_{sk}\), and set \(v_{ti}=w_{stk}^{1/2}b_r(u_{stk})\).  Then
\[
G=\sum_{t,i}v_{ti}v_{ti}^\top,
\qquad
a_{stik}=w_{stk}^{1/2}e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
&\le
\left\{\sum_{t,i}(e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\{e_0^\top G^{-1}GG^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}\mathsf L^{1/2}
=\{\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}.
\tag{43}
\end{aligned}
\]
The selector requires \(G/\mathsf L\succeq c_GI\), so \(G^{-1}\preceq(c_G\mathsf L)^{-1}I\).  Under the declared monomial normalization, \(e_0=b_r(0)\) is the constant-monomial coordinate and \(\|e_0\|_2=1\).  Hence
\[
\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\le c_G^{-1}.
\tag{44}
\]
For fixed \((s,t,k)\), neither \(u_{stk}\) nor \(w_{stk}\) depends on \(i\), while
\[
G=n_s\sum_tw_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^\top.
\]
Thus \(a_{stik}\) is constant in \(i\), and (43)--(44) imply
\[
\sum_t|a_{stik}|\le\frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}.
\tag{45}
\]
The triangle inequality after averaging the fixed donor folds gives \(\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\le c_G^{-1/2}/n_s\).  Therefore
\[
\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le\sum_sn_s\left(\frac{\pi_sc_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}\right)^2
=c_G^{-1}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{46}
\]

Finally, the normal equations reproduce every polynomial of total degree at most \(r\).  Subtract the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\), use \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} in the form
\[
|m_s(x)-T_{r,\widetilde z_{sk}}m_s(x)|
\le C_{r,d}L\|x-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
and sum the absolute weighted remainders.  Cohort weighting and fold averaging give precisely the definition of \(A_L\).  No upper bound on \(L_{sk}\) is used.

Condition on \((E_0,\widetilde z_{sk})\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-independence} implies that this conditioning leaves the conditional historical design law and its beta-mixing envelope unchanged.  For \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(h\in(0,1]\), define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
The kernel conditions, \texttt{ass:design-density}, fixed dimension and degree, and a change of variables give constants \(c_0,C_0>0\) such that, uniformly in \(z,h\) and unit \(v\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\),
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d,
\qquad
\mathbb E[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]\ge c_0h^d.
\tag{47}
\]
The one-sided intersection with the cube is harmless: \(K\) is positive on a neighborhood of zero, and a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on a set with interior.  Compactness of the unit sphere and the rescaled cube intersections makes the lower bound uniform.  Choose \(c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Let \(b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil\), with \(C_\beta\) large enough that
\[
T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A}.
\tag{48}
\]
Partition calendar indices into consecutive blocks of length \(b_T\) and split the blocks by parity.  Blocks within either parity are separated by at least \(b_T\) indices.  The definition of absolute regularity and the overlap coupling of two probability measures couple each parity family to independent blocks, by induction, with total mismatch probability at most
\[
C(T/b_T)\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le CT^{-A}.
\tag{49}
\]

For a parity family and \(F=\ell_{z,h}\) or \(F=v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\), let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) in block \(g\).  Uniform boundedness gives \(0\le W_g\le Cb_T\), and \(W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g\).  Hence, for the independent coupled blocks,
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
\le Cb_T\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g]
\le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{50}
\]
Expanding each centered exponential series, using \(|W_g-\mathbb EW_g|\le Cb_T\) for terms of order at least two, multiplying the independent moment generating functions, and optimizing the Chernoff exponent yields the bounded-block Bernstein bound
\[
P\left\{\left|\sum_g(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)\right|>cTh^d\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{51}
\]
Adding (49) gives (51) plus \(CT^{-A}\) for the original blocks.

Apply (51) to local mass and to the quadratic forms of the local Gram matrix on a fixed \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  The net cardinality is fixed because \(q_r\) is fixed.  Approximation of a minimum-eigenvalue eigenvector by the net, together with boundedness of \(b_r\) on the kernel support, turns the net inequalities into a matrix inequality.  Applying the same bound to the mass denominator and using (47) gives
\[
P\left\{L_{sk}(h)=0\ \text{or}\
\lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{G_{sk}(h)}{L_{sk}(h)}\right)<c_G
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A}.
\tag{52}
\]
Replicated rows multiply \(G_{sk}(h)\) and \(L_{sk}(h)\) by the same factor \(n_s\), so they do not affect the normalized shape test.

The log-adjusted definition of \(h_{s,\beta}\) and a sufficiently large \(C_h\) imply
\[
\frac{T(2^vh_{s,\beta})^d}{b_T}\ge c2^{vd}.
\tag{53}
\]
If the selector has not stopped by \(2^vh_{s,\beta}\), that candidate fails; (52)--(53) prove the asserted tail.  At \(h=1\), (52) gives terminal failure probability at most
\[
C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}.
\tag{54}
\]

For any fixed \(a>0\), the dyadic tail-sum formula gives
\[
\mathbb E[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}]
\le h_{s,\beta}^a
+\sum_{v:2^vh_{s,\beta}<1}
(2^{v+1}h_{s,\beta})^aP\{h_{sk}>2^vh_{s,\beta}\}.
\]
The series \(\sum_v2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}\) converges.  Because the dyadic values are capped at one, the \(T^{-A}\) contribution is \(O(T^{-A})\), which is absorbed by the displayed three-term rate for the chosen \(A\).  This proves the moment assertion.

For fixed \(S,K_D\), a union bound in (54) controls all fits.  Donor complements are nonempty eventually; successful-fit weights and radii are finite; spectral clipping of a finite sample covariance is a defined measurable operation; and \(\max_k\delta_k\le\delta_0\) eventually because \(m_k\asymp N\).  Thus the total bad probability is at most the right side of (54), and this is \(O(R_{\star,\beta})\).  Finally, the uninflated smoothing component can have \(T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d=O(1)\), but the definition of \(h_{s,\beta}\) gives
\[
Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2).
\]
This is the concentration actually used in (53).  No dense-local-site or upper-local-mass condition has been imposed.

Fix an interior \(z_0\) and a sufficiently small \(c_p>0\).  Let
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L>0\) is so small that \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\).  Then, after decreasing \(c_p\) if necessary,
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{55}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at \(z_0\), contained in the cube, with Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  Its radius obeys
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{56}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently over blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the block's design points independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  Since \(\operatorname{Leb}_d(A_T)=p_T\), each one-time marginal density equals
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{57}
\]
Thus the density bounds hold after choosing their fixed envelope to contain one.

Sigma-fields separated by at least \(L_T\) depend on disjoint independent block variables.  At a smaller lag only a shared block can induce dependence.  Conditional on its binary state the two separated parts are independent; expansion of this two-component mixture bounds its absolute-regularity distance from the product law by \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Therefore (55) implies
\[
\beta_P(k\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le k<L_T,\\
0,&k\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^k.
\tag{58}
\]

Choose a bounded Holder carrier \(g\) in the interior of the response range.  For \(\lambda>1\), give \(g\) a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\); for \(0<\lambda\le1\), give it an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there.  Rescale it so its covariance-standardized modulus lies strictly between the declared lower and upper constants.  For a smooth bump \(\psi\) supported on the unit ball with \(\psi(0)=1\), set
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda\psi((x-z_0)/h_T).
\tag{59}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_b>0\), both functions lie in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and the response interior.  If \(\lambda>1\), the perturbation's increment is at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\); it therefore cannot cancel the carrier's affine lower modulus.  If \(0<\lambda\le1\), its increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so it cannot cancel a fixed cusp lower modulus when \(c_b\) is small.  The Holder upper bound supplies the upper modulus.  Thus both laws obey \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Given the complete design, draw bounded errors independently across units, centered conditional on that design, with conditional variance at least \(B^{-1}\), and set historical response mean to \(m_\ell(X_{st})\) under law \(\ell\).  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of the design with a common mean under both laws.  Complete untreated event potential outcomes with cohort-average mean \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{60}
\]
Hold all other cohorts, donors, and potential outcomes fixed across the laws and complete them inside the frozen envelopes.  Equations (57)--(60), together with consistency, no spillovers, limited anticipation, exact training coordinates, and event transport, place both laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  With \(T/L_T+O(1)\) blocks,
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{61}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), all design points lie outside \(A_T\), where the regressions in (59) agree.  The complete observed-data laws coincide there, so
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{62}
\]
The observed event mean is common, while event transport changes the untreated event mean by \(c_bh_T^\lambda\).  Substitution of these two facts directly into \texttt{def:target}, for a fixed positive-weight cohort, gives
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{63}
\]
The two-point squared-error calculation applied to (62)--(63) yields the \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) minimax lower bound.  Decreasing \(c_p\) makes the affinity in (62) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\); integrating simultaneous coverage against the overlap measure yields the \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\) expected-length lower bound.  The construction uses no sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering premise.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(h_{sk}\) be selected by the normalized-shape rule in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  For a sufficiently large fixed initial-scale constant and some fixed \(A>2\lambda/d+2\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), every donor fold, every cohort, and every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_{s,\beta}\le1\),
\[
P\{h_{sk}>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A}.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}]
\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}
+\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}
+N^{-a/2}\right\}.
\]
The terminal-grid failure probability is at most \(C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}\), and the total bad-sample probability in \texttt{def:honest-interval} is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the stated arrays.  These bounds remain valid when the uninflated smoothing-scale local count \(T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d\) is \(O(1)\); the selected log-adjusted initial scale itself satisfies \(Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2)\).  No exogenous dense-local-site or upper-local-mass condition is imposed.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old final sentence incorrectly attached the \(O(1)\) local-count possibility to the selected log-adjusted scale.  The proof allows an \(O(1)\) count only at the uninflated smoothing scale; the selected initial scale has count at least a constant times \(\log(T\vee2)\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For the maintained geometrically beta-mixing class, define
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)},
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa},
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
For \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), \(R_q\) denotes respectively \(R_{\mathrm{tr}},R_{\mathrm{sm}},R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},R_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Retain
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d},
\qquad
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\]
only as the iid-design comparator, or comparator under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The construction must record \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), \(R_{\star,\beta}\), and the channel routing for the maintained geometric-mixing class, while describing \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) only as an iid-design comparator, or comparator under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw \(\widehat\tau\).  This equality is identified under event transport.  The sharp conditional-risk rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and the uniformly honest expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\) hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), which imposes the two stated full-design centering restrictions.  The donor component remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus, and no sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering condition is imposed.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The old metadata names the iid-comparator frontier and says the applied same-class theorem remains unproved; the completed proofs establish the log-adjusted frontier over the full-design-centered subclass.

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path.  Consistency and a maintained cohort-average event-transport restriction identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator is exactly an event coefficient in a foldwise weighted panel regression.  Over the explicitly restricted full-design-centered class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), matching lower and upper bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and uniformly honest expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Geometric beta mixing and marginal density alone yield the unavoidable spacing term \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); a rare-block witness rules out the iid spacing rate uniformly without an additional anti-clustering condition.  The feasible full-data interval combines separate bounded cluster-level Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and a fourth-moment donor-modulus allowance.  The donor channel saturates at \(N^{-1}\) in mean squared error when \(\lambda>1\), conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory mainly treats linear return contrasts; repeated-measurement regression fixes the query; generated-regressor theory typically moves training coordinates; and synthetic-control inference does not deliver a generated-event-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth under arbitrary relative growth.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture here observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, and generated-center uncertainty without a classical measurement-error inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact weighted-panel coefficient representation, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers over the transparent full-design-centered subclass.  A normalized Gram-shape selector, full-data cluster-level Hoeffding calibration, exact Taylor allowance, covariance-standardized donor control, and four channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish the result without sequential overlap or an upper local-mass condition.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero.  Their calendar process is geometrically beta mixing; this permits logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and therefore entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and a fourth-moment envelope; historical training coordinates are exact.  Fixed-fold projected donor means feed a log-adjusted local-polynomial fit selected by normalized Gram shape.  The interval uses the full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event cluster-level Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and a donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared bad sample.

prose_updates.interpretation: The active risk is, up to fixed constants, the maximum of treated-cohort averaging noise, log-adjusted calendar spacing, and generated-donor uncertainty; the replicated-smoothing term is retained for bookkeeping but cannot be uniquely active.  The oracle region has donor error asymptotically smaller than the other active terms, the generated-proxy region has it larger, and the boundary equates \(N^{-\kappa}\) with their maximum.  The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality.  The risk and honest-length theorems additionally use the two explicit strong full-design strict-exogeneity and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence.  The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass.  The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp constants.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of the event-transport identification formula, exact raw-estimator FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, log-adjusted geometric-mixing selector bound, positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, four channelwise causal-panel embeddings, and matching conditional risk and uniformly honest expected-length frontiers over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  No sequential-overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, event conditional-variance, studentization, or temporal-within-unit independence condition is added.  The same-class logarithmic spacing term is unavoidable under the maintained assumptions.  The iid rate is only a stricter-design comparator.  The donor converse is conditional on the two-sided local modulus, and all causal interpretation remains conditional on event transport.

statement_notes.gap: These bounds remain valid when the uninflated smoothing-scale local count \(T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d\) is \(O(1)\); the selected log-adjusted initial scale itself satisfies \(Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2)\).  No exogenous dense-local-site or upper-local-mass condition is imposed.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
 \qquad
 q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
We first derive the scalar inequality used below.  For \(u>0\), let
\(\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a\).  Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
 \phi'(u)=a(1-u^{a-1}).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on
\((1,\infty)\).  Hence \(\phi(u)\geq 0\) for every \(u>0\).  Substitution of
\(u=x/y\), followed by multiplication by \(y>0\), gives
\[
 x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
 \qquad x,y>0.
\]
The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give \(q(1-a)=a\).  Therefore, for each
cohort \(s\), positivity of \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits the preceding inequality
with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\), yielding
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}
 \leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\]
Since \(T\geq1\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Thus the corrected
spacing definition in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} implies
\[
 T^{-q}
 \leq (\log2)^{-q}
 \left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
 =(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Multiplying the cohortwise bound by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), and using
\(\sum_s\pi_s^2\leq(\sum_s\pi_s)^2=1\), which follows from positivity and
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)T^{-q}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2\\
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
 &\leq C_{\lambda,d}
   \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}
 =\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
 +\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log2)^{-2\lambda/d}\geq1.
\]
Let
\[
 A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
 \qquad
 D:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
The corrected frontier definition and the preceding display imply, equation by
equation,
\[
 D\leq R_{\star,\beta}
 =A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}D.
\]
The last inequality uses \(C_{\lambda,d}\geq1\).  This proves
\(R_{\star,\beta}\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), uniformly
in the positive sample sizes; the comparison constants do not depend on
\(N\), \(T\), or \(\mathbf n\).

By \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\), whereas
\(A\) is independent of \(N\).  Consequently the donor contribution is
asymptotically negligible exactly in the oracle region
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates exactly in the generated-center region
\[
 A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
Equality up to positive constants, \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\), is equivalent,
because \(\kappa>0\), to
\[
 N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
These comparisons become minimax phases whenever a separate sharp-risk theorem
establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) for the experiment in question.

Under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query
local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers
\(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\), the comparator in
\texttt{def:rate-frontier} applies.  The same cohortwise inequality, without
the logarithmic comparison, gives
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
 \leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
The comparator definition of \(R_\star\) therefore yields the exact identity
\[
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} states
\(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Hence using the recorded historical
coordinate does not require inversion of a measurement-error convolution.
Inspection of \texttt{def:rate-frontier} then confirms that its bookkeeping has
no deconvolution component and no separately postulated moving-Gram rate.  This
is an algebraic and observation-structure conclusion, not an independent
sharpness claim.  Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\); thus \(\lambda>1\)
implies \(\kappa=1\), and the donor term is
\(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\), proving higher-smoothness saturation.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\) and all positive sample sizes, let
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
 +\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log2)^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
Then
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \qquad
 R_{\star,\beta}
 \asymp_{\lambda,d}
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently, in any experiment for which \(R_{\star,\beta}\) is established
as the sharp risk, the oracle region is
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\]
the generated-center region is
\[
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=o(N^{-\kappa}),
\]
and the boundary is
\[
 N\asymp
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query
local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers
\(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), one instead has the exact relations
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
 \qquad
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} removes a classical
measurement-error inverse problem from the historical design; accordingly the
defined bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate
moving-Gram rate.  Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever
\(\lambda>1\).  These algebraic conclusions do not by themselves assert that
either frontier is sharp for a statistical experiment.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original uniform claim uses the no-logarithm comparator frontier. Under geometric beta mixing and marginal density alone, the uniformly valid frontier has the logarithmic spacing component. In addition, a fixed query alone does not deliver the comparator spacing rate; the fixed-query comparator requires a separately imposed local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Define
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d},
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Here \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\(R_{\mathrm{sm}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and
\(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\).  Retain
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d},
\qquad
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\]
only as the iid-design comparator, or comparator under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), let \(R_q\) denote respectively \(R_{\mathrm{tr}},R_{\mathrm{sm}},R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},R_{\mathrm{don}}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The corrected construction preserves the geometric-mixing frontier and the complete channel routing, while repairing the overly broad fixed-query comparator label: a fixed query must be accompanied by a local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition to deliver the no-logarithm spacing term.
